thesis: Millstone gave control decks a repeatable win condition that ignored life totals and eventually lent its name to the entire strategy of milling libraries.

canonicalIdentity.identityNotes: Original Antiquities 1994-03-04 credited to Kaja Foglio; printing ID remains from accepted snapshot. Modern Oracle text is not misidentified as original printed wording. Verified focused mechanics source: https://mtg.wtf/card/atq/56/Millstone

originalContext.designPurpose: Millstone changes the library, not the player's hand. Its two-mana tap activation mills two cards from the top of one targeted player's library into their graveyard; winning by decking still requires that player to attempt a draw from an empty library.
